title: You Could Fit In Its Mouth. You'd Never Fit Down Its Throat.

scenes.notes: You'd fit inside a blue whale's mouth. It still couldn't swallow you.

scenes.notes: This is the heaviest animal ever measured. Up to thirty metres long. That's two and a half city buses, parked nose to tail.
It can weigh close to two hundred tonnes. Heavier than the biggest dinosaurs we've ever dug up.
Its tongue alone weighs about as much as an elephant.

scenes.notes: Its heart is the size of a golf cart. And on a deep dive, that heart can slow down to just two beats a minute.

scenes.notes: Its call is louder than a jet engine, and it can carry for hundreds of kilometres.
To eat, it charges into a cloud of krill and takes one gulp of water bigger than its own body.
So what happens to you, floating right in the middle of that cloud?

scenes.notes: Here's the surprising part. It eats up to forty million krill a day, and every one is tiny. Its throat only opens about as wide as a beach ball. Anything bigger just gets pushed back out.

scenes.notes: The real danger isn't being eaten. It's being in the way when two hundred tonnes decides to turn, and a tail seven metres wide sweeps past.
Room for you in its mouth. No room down its throat. And it would barely notice you were there.
